title: Take an incident from intake to closeout

scenes.title: Take an incident from intake to closeout
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will take an incident from intake to closeout. Inconsistent call classification and unclear recipients create avoidable re-entry and uncertainty during dispatch. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: A department adds Structure Fire and Medical call types, sets Responding and On Scene statuses and connects its county CAD email feed. Consistent call types and statuses make dispatching, response tracking and reporting reliable from the first call. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Call types and priorities
scenes.narration: Call types and priorities. The call types and priorities used to classify calls. Add the call types your dispatchers use and set their priorities.

scenes.title: Personnel and unit statuses
scenes.narration: Personnel and unit statuses. The statuses members and units report, such as Responding or On Scene. Review the built-in statuses and add your own where your terms differ.

scenes.title: Dispatch Settings
scenes.narration: Dispatch Settings. How calls page personnel: by group or by shift, and related automatic status changes. Choose whether dispatch follows groups or shifts, and review the automatic status options.

scenes.title: Email and CAD call intake
scenes.narration: Email and CAD call intake. Create calls automatically from CAD, paging or email dispatches. Choose your CAD or paging format and connect the mailbox that receives dispatches.

scenes.title: Run cards and recommendations
scenes.narration: Run cards and recommendations. Recommended resources for each call type or area. Build run cards for your most common calls, then turn on recommendations.

scenes.title: Calls
scenes.narration: Calls. Active calls and their dispatch status. Collect your call types, the statuses members report while responding, and the details of any CAD or paging system that should create calls.

scenes.title: New Call
scenes.narration: New Call. Create and dispatch a call. Collect your call types, the statuses members report while responding, and the details of any CAD or paging system that should create calls.

scenes.title: Archived Calls
scenes.narration: Archived Calls. Closed and past calls. Collect your call types, the statuses members report while responding, and the details of any CAD or paging system that should create calls.

scenes.title: Call templates
scenes.narration: Call templates. Reusable call text and note templates that speed up call entry. Collect your call types, the statuses members report while responding, and the details of any CAD or paging system that should create calls.

scenes.title: Check-in timers
scenes.narration: Check-in timers. Timers that remind responders on a call to check in, with escalation when they do not. Collect your call types, the statuses members report while responding, and the details of any CAD or paging system that should create calls.

scenes.title: Text call intake and commands
scenes.narration: Text call intake and commands. Create calls and accept member commands by text message. Collect your call types, the statuses members report while responding, and the details of any CAD or paging system that should create calls.

scenes.title: Call Settings
scenes.narration: Call Settings. The mailbox and format used to import calls from CAD or paging email. Collect your call types, the statuses members report while responding, and the details of any CAD or paging system that should create calls.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Configure call types, priorities, and response statuses. Step 2. Create a training call, confirm its map location, and choose recipients. Step 3. Review response progress, close the training call, and find it in archived calls.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Check the saved call details and intended recipients. Use a controlled communication test to evaluate delivery separately from the saved dispatch. A common problem to watch for: Run-card recommendations require review. Shift routing, unit crew routing, group routing, and automatic status changes can affect different people.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Create a Medical training call for Station 1. Confirm the location, recipients, status transitions, closeout, and archived record. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed.
